title: Adam DeVine Reveals His Worst Holiday Gift

 Larry Stansbury Sun, 15 November 2026 at 6:30 pm UTC 3 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Adam DeVine Reveals His Worst Holiday Gift Adam DeVine is not pretending to be a holiday-shopping expert.
 In Macy's holiday campaign, the actor plays a notoriously bad gift-giver. During an exclusive interview with Men's Journal , DeVine admitted the role was an example of accurate casting.
 "I'm a pretty garbage gift giver," he said. "It's not because I don't love my friends and family. I'm just late at buying gifts."
 His most memorable failure involved his father, who worked for the railroad. In his 20s, DeVine decided a wooden whistle that sounded like a train would make a thoughtful present.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "He opened it up and goes, 'What the hell is this?'" DeVine recalled. "He goes, 'I hate working for the railroad.'"
 The experience made DeVine's lesson from the Macy's partnership fairly straightforward: Ask for help. Instead of waiting until the last minute and panic-buying another wooden whistle, he recommends seeking guidance from someone who can steer shoppers toward a gift the recipient will actually use.
 DeVine's curated Macy's list spans grooming, fashion, home and family gifts. His selections include the Kiehl's Merry & Well-Groomed Gift Set , Dior Sauvage Extrait , a gold-tone Movado Bold Verso watch , the Ninja Crispi Pro , Nike Tech Fleece , and a Breville Barista Express .
 The campaign also paired DeVine with Melissa Joan Hart. As someone who grew up watching Clarissa Explains It All and Sabrina the Teenage Witch , he was excited to finally work with her. However, the campaign's tightly structured spots left limited space for improvisation.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Now in his 40s, DeVine said his personal wish list has become more practical. He would gladly receive an eyebrow trimmer to manage his increasingly "wiry eyebrows," even if he might pretend to be offended when opening it.
 His strongest grooming recommendation for other men is even simpler.
 "I've been moisturizing," DeVine said. "I'll apply a little moisturizer in the morning. And then I have a heavier cream that my wife bought me at nighttime. Dude, I'm doubly moisturized."
 Fragrance remains an unresolved part of his routine. Despite selecting Dior Sauvage for his Macy's gift guide, DeVine said he has never considered himself a cologne guy and has historically relied on what he jokingly called his "natural stank."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement This year, he wants his wife to help him find a signature fragrance that she finds attractive.
 "I don't want to be one of those old guys that smells like an old person," he said. "I'm ready to have a signature fragrance."
 His wife has already convinced him to embrace another holiday ritual: matching family pajamas. DeVine initially resisted coordinating outfits, but his opinion changed after becoming a father.
 "The photos, when we're all dressed the same, are cute AF," he admitted.
 The most thoughtful gift DeVine has received was a watch from his wife when they married. He wears it regularly, and checking the time reminds him of her.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Ultimately, DeVine's favorite holiday tradition has little to do with presents. His relatives gather under one roof, even if that means sleeping on couches and inflatable mattresses.
 "It's kind of chaos for the few days that everybody's together," he said. "But it's fun because it makes you feel like everybody's a little kid again."
